subject: use the posterior as the prior

messages.author: b8138de0d37a5dbb
messages.subject: use the posterior as the prior
parts:
Hello Everyone,

I would highly appreciate any help with this problem.

I am trying to estimate the parameters of a stochastic dynamical model from real time series ECG signal. First I tried the estimation from 10 cycles but this didn't work. Then, I tried the estimation from 1 cycle and the estimation was more accurate. The idea is that instead of fitting all the data in one go, I will fit some of the data, get a posterior, and then fit the next cycle using the posterior from the previous fit as the prior. I am using MATLAB-STAN. One limitation is that I need to update the stan file after each fit and recompile it again. Is there a better approach to do this job ???

Thanks & regards,
Kamal

messages.author: df2011c04ce6269d
messages.subject: Re: use the posterior as the prior
parts:
Assuming your data x follows blah distribution and you sampled parameter alpha K times in previous phase.
Use previous sampled parameters as another data to build a posterior distribution.

pseudo codes here:
functions{
  real update_alpha_log(posterior_alpha, vector[M] prior_alpha[K]){
    ...
  }
  real blah_log(vector[N] x, vector[M] alpha){
    ...
  }
}
data{
  bool build_posterior_from_prior;
  vector[M] prior_alpha[K];
  vector[N] x;
}
parameters{
  vector[M] posterior_alpha;
}
model{
  if(build_posterior_from_prior){
    posterior_alpha ~ update_alpha(prior_alpha);
  }
  x ~ blah(posterior_alpha);
}

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] use the posterior as the prior
parts:
We keep getting questions in pairs; this matches the
one I just responded to on doing sequential inference with
fake data for power calculations.

In both cases, it'll be more efficient to just model everything
jointly. If it doesn't work to fit jointly, there's a good
chance something's wrong with the model itself.

When you say 10 cycles didn't work, what do you mean?

- Bob

Hi,

I am trying to fit some of the data, get a posterior, and then fit the next segment of data using the posterior from the previous fit as the prior. I am using stochastic dynamical model for ECG.
Is it possible to find the mean and variance of the sampled parameter values and then use them in the definition of the probability distribution for the prior (assuming its Normal) for the next phase?

Thanks,
Kamal

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: use the posterior as the prior
parts:
Yes, you can compute these directly from the sample
draws. There’s no built-in way to do this, but it’s
an easy calculation in any interface (other than CmdStan).

- Bob
